https://nineoclock.ro/romanian-president.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount President Nicușor Dan Highlights Romanian-French Strategic Partnership on France’s National Day Bucharest, July 15, 2026 – President Nicușor Dan underscored the strength of the Romanian-French Strategic Partnership and the longstanding friendship between the two countries in a message published on his official X account after attending France’s National Day celebrations in Paris at the invitation of French President Emmanuel Macron. France’s National Day celebrations in Paris The Romanian head of state described his participation in the Bastille Day ceremonies as a special moment, noting that this year’s celebrations coincide with the centennial of the French-Romanian Friendship Treaty, an important milestone in bilateral relations. According to President Dan, the anniversary provides an opportunity to reaffirm the Strategic Partnership between Romania and France, built on close political dialogue, expanding economic cooperation and strong security ties within the Euro-Atlantic framework. A symbolic highlight of this year’s celebrations was the participation of soldiers from Romania’s 30th Guard Brigade “Mihai Viteazul” in the traditional military parade on the Champs-Élysées. Marching alongside French troops and military contingents from allied and partner countries, the Romanian Guard’s presence reflected the close defence cooperation between Bucharest and Paris and the solidarity shared by NATO allies. President Dan described the participation of the Romanian servicemen as another tangible demonstration of the friendship between the two nations and of their commitment to common security objectives. Romania and France have developed one of the closest strategic partnerships in the European Union and NATO, cooperating extensively in the fields of defence, energy, infrastructure, education and economic development. France also plays a key role in NATO’s enhanced Forward Presence in Romania, contributing to the security of NATO’s Eastern Flank. President Nicușor Dan’s full statement, as published on X: “It is with a very special pleasure that I join, on this July 14 in Paris, the ceremonies of France’s National Day, at the invitation of President Emmanuel Macron. In this centennial year of the French-Romanian Friendship Treaty, we thus reaffirm our Strategic Partnership and the privileged friendship between Romania and France, founded on deepened cooperation at the political, economic, and security levels. I am happy and proud that the soldiers of the 30th Guard Brigade “Mihai Viteazul” are participating, alongside their French comrades and those of many other allied and partner countries, in the Champs-Élysées parade. This is yet further proof of Romanian-French friendship and our allied solidarity.” France’s National Day celebrations in Paris Mihai Manea, Publisher, Nine O’Clock / Social Media: LinkedIn | Facebook | Instagram 🗂 Explore our Digital Edition archives available in more than 150 countries (2024–2025–2026): · 📰 Daily Archives Nine o’clock (Romania) Daily Archives · 📖 Weekly Archives Nine o’clock Weekly (Romania) Archives · 📚 Yearbook Magazine Nine o’clock Yearbook (Romania) Magazine Social media Nine O`Clock: Pagina LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/nineoclock Pagina Facebook https://www.facebook.com/nineoclockromania/ Pagina Instagram https://www.instagram.com/nineoclockro/ Pagina Twitter https://twitter.com/Nine O’Clock The diplomatic daily newspaper Nine O’Clock does not assume responsibility for the information received and published on the public website. The Center, according to a news release, will act as an “educational destination dedicated to preserving Jewish history, teaching the lessons of the Holocaust and helping our community better understand the history and continued impact of antisemitism.” Guests in attendance at the ceremonious unveiling of the Center also heard from educators in the Classroom Without Borders initiative, which sees educators traveling to Poland to study the Holocaust where it happened. Teachers who shared their experiences on the trip include: Rebecca Baxter, Champion Local School District Diana Ferrell, Union Area School District Timothy Nowery, Bristol Local School District Brian Bugos, Newton Falls Exempted Village Schools Bugos is noted to have been the chaperone for six high school students who also participated in the Classroom Without Borders initiative. The Center will house over 5,000 books related to the Holocaust, the Dr. Saul Friedman Holocaust Research Audio Collection and a permanent Antisemitism Timeline, which traces over 2,000 years of anti-Jewish hate. The Dr. Saul Friedman collection looks to preserve the voices and testimonies of Holocaust Survivors. The Center also features a commissioned mural by Andrew Merritt, titled “The Staff of Resilience.” Anyone looking to visit the Center can do so during the Jewish Community Center’s regular operating hours between 5:30 a.m. and 9 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 5:30 a.m to 7 p.m. on Friday and 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday. Holiday hours vary. Download the WFMJ app for your Apple or Android smartphone or tablet to get our push alerts as news happens. https://www.theguardian.com/world/video/.text: 0:57 Cyprus Helicopters and boats rescue passengers from capsized ferry in northern Cyprus – video Passengers of a capsized ship off the coast of Cyprus were seen being rescued by passing vessels and coastguard authorities. Helicopters and boats brought survivors back to shore from the ferry that was carrying around 270 passengers and crew. At least eight people are confirmed to have died and nearly 20 remain missing. Search teams and divers are looking for more survivors in deep waters and it is currently unclear if people remained trapped on the vessel. https://www.politico.eu/article/germanys.text: BRUSSELS — Volkswagen’s growing crisis — with the company proposing factory closures and thousands of layoffs — is turning into political rocket fuel for the far-right Alternative for Germany party ahead of Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt. “The end of traditional German car plants is the result of a failed economic and energy policy,” Tino Chrupalla, AfD’s federal spokesperson, said in a statement, putting the blame on the coalition government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume is going before the automaker’s board on Friday in his latest bid to push through a sweeping cost-cutting plan that would slash 100,000 jobs, along with closing four German factories — action the company has never before taken. Advertisement Advertisement The deepening crisis at Germany's largest company comes at a terrible time for Merz, who promised to reform the economy and revitalize the country’s industrial base when he took power in 2025. Instead, automotive suppliers, chemical companies and other manufacturing firms are bleeding jobs, energy prices are high and the country is facing a growing wave of Chinese exports that threaten to gut important industries. All of those worries are coalescing around VW, an industrial powerhouse that employs over 280,000 people in Germany. “The crisis at VW is affecting the mood across the whole country. VW embodies German social capitalism like no other company,” said Klaus Dörre, a German sociologist specializing in right-wing populism and industrial transitions. Unions and politicians are threatening resistance in case Blume goes through with his promised cuts. "We will not agree to any strategy that presents plant closures and the reduction of industrial jobs as a supposedly easy solution," said a spokesperson for Olaf Lies, the Social Democratic Party premier of Lower Saxony, where Volkswagen is headquartered. Advertisement Advertisement Politicians from Lower Saxony, including Lies, sit on the supervisory board along with members of the powerful IG Metall union, making any restructuring difficult to push through. The union is threatening a fight. “The factory floor will burn at all locations — I tell you that. We will oppose it with all our might. We will not allow our sites to bleed out,” Thorsten Gröger, IG Metall’s district manager for Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, said at a meeting between union representatives and German politicians on Aug. 31. That mood is helping the AfD, which is within striking distance of winning an outright majority in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday. Such a win would give a far-right party governing power in a German state for the first time since World War II. The AfD is similarly on the rise in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — both holding elections this month. "No chancellor has driven the economic misery and deindustrialization of our country as much as Friedrich Merz," said AfD co-chair Alice Weidel in a statement . Advertisement Advertisement Political gain from business pain While there is no VW plant in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right party is seeking to capitalize on a growing national panic about the automaker's fate and the decline of German industrial might. The AfD blames the auto sector’s decline on Merz and on the EU’s climate agenda, which initially proposed banning new combustion-engine vehicles starting in 2035. The European Commission walked back the measure in December, but negotiations are continuing in Brussels over what emission-reduction targets automakers must reach or face fines. The EU plan has been unpopular with German voters since it was first proposed — and Merz also opposes it — but the AfD is leaning heavily into the 2035 legislation to show Brussels as being hostile to German industry and Merz as too feckless to block the measure. “The one-sided and premature fixation on electromobility has led Germany's key industry into a dead end,” Chrupalla said. However, any changes to the EU's rules will not fix Volkswagen’s real problem: China. The country was once VW's biggest and most profitable market, helping subsidize factories back home. The shift to electric vehicles and competition from Chinese automakers making very good cars at low prices have flipped the scales. VW’s China sales dropped 26 percent year-over-year in the first six months of this year. Advertisement Advertisement The shift to electric cars is also endangering VW's traditional dominance in combustion engines. VW and other European carmakers are scrambling to catch up to Chinese companies that have better EV technology and dominate the global battery market. They're also grappling with high labor costs and with the enormous price tag of retooling their factories for EVs — something Blume is hoping to address with his reform plans. But the AfD isn't spending much time on the intricacies of China's industrial rise. Instead, it's pointing the finger at its political rivals. The AfD is "skillfully exploiting" the threat of job cuts and factory closures “to blame the alleged ‘climate-driven planned economy’ for the crisis in the car industry and the entire economic model,” said Dörre. “This resonates well with sections of the working class, not least because they cannot afford an electric car themselves.” With lawmakers across the political spectrum and workers staunchly opposing the cost-cutting measure, Blume is unlikely to get his proposal accepted on Friday. It’s an outcome that would delay negotiations closer to elections in Lower Saxony in September of next year. That puts even more pressure on the state’s lawmakers to fight any plant closures as they try to fend off the AfD, which was just behind the Christian Democrats and the Social Democrats in a poll taken earlier this year. Advertisement Advertisement "For me as prime minister, it is inconceivable that we will no longer build cars here,” said Lies. But that fight may come too late to slow a surging AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, where one poll by the INSA organization shows the party has the support of 43 percent of respondents, far ahead of the Christian Democrats with 22 percent and close to the level needed for an outright majority in the state parliament. Romanus Otte contributed reporting from Berlin .

It comes during the final week in which Romania can still hit its remaining targets under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan agreed with the European Commission. Senators are debating the Hydrogen Law under emergency procedure, a crucial milestone without which the country risks losing a 2.84-billion-Euro payout. In parallel, deputies must re-examine the Integrity Law, modified following objections by the Constitutional Court, alongside new rules for high school entrance exams. Meanwhile, the adoption of the new public sector salary law remains uncertain, another major milestone on which 770 million Euro depend. Although the deadline is August 31, the draft is still being analyzed by political parties following discussions with President Nicușor Dan. So far, only the Liberals have backed the latest version of the proposal, which faces fierce contestation from trade unions. New measures to restart the Cernavodă NPP Romanian authorities are taking new emergency measures to restart the nuclear power plant at Cernavodă, located in the southeast of the country along the Danube. The Ministry of Energy and Hidroelectrica are working to increase the river’s flow to ensure the water necessary for cooling the reactors. At the entry point into the country at Baziaș, in the southwest, the Danube’s flow is three times lower than the normal average for this period, measuring just 1,300 cubic meters per second compared to the usual 3,900. Under these conditions, the National Committee for Emergency Situations has already begun releasing large volumes of water from reservoirs along the Olt River. In addition, dredging operations continue. Although Cernavodă has backup deep wells, operating the nuclear reactors at maximum capacity depends on the high flow rate that only the Danube can supply. Currently, Romania is importing electricity daily at high prices. Romania reports highest EU fuel price spike Data from Eurostat shows Romania recorded the highest fuel price increase in the European Union over the past 12 months. The largest rate spikes for gasoline and diesel were registered in Romania at 24%, followed by Germany, Lithuania, and Bulgaria at around 22%. At the opposite end, the smallest price increases were recorded in Sweden at 1.2% and Ireland at 3%. The only country where prices dropped year-over-year in July 2026 compared to July 2025 was Hungary, with a slight dip of 0.1%. Looking at month-on-month figures for Romania, Eurostat notes diesel prices rose in July by 4.6% compared to June, while gasoline prices fell by 0.8%. Romanian firefighters deploy to extinguish wildfires in Serbia Romanian firefighters have begun operations to extinguish wildfires in neighboring Serbia. So far, the 69 responders from nine Romanian counties have prepared the ground for upcoming interventions, the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations announced on Sunday. They met with local authorities, identified water sources, and conducted reconnaissance missions. A Romanian helicopter is also participating in the action, having executed seven water drops over the affected areas since Saturday. The flames are primarily raging in Serbia’s Deliblato Sands reserve, approximately 20 km from Romania, where over 3,500 hectares have been burning for more than a week. Smoke has also reached towns in western Romania as well as the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. Serbia activated the European Union’s Civil Protection Mechanism, leading to the deployment of Romanian and German firefighters, along with helicopters from Romania, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia. National Bank warns political uncertainty and twin deficits pose risks to the Leu Uncertainties stemming from the domestic political situation pose a risk to the exchange rate of the Romanian Leu, the National Bank warns in the minutes of its latest monetary policy meeting. According to the BNR, other significant risks stem from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and, above all, Romania’s lingering twin deficits, the budget deficit and the trade deficit, which occurs when a country imports more than it exports. In this context, the Central Bank stresses the importance of political and governmental stability, as well as the need to maintain fiscal consolidation to reduce both deficits. On Friday, during the week’s final trading session, the national currency depreciated against the Euro, with the National Bank calculating the rate at nearly 5.26 lei. Moldovan Prime Minister swims across the Bosphorus Strait in symbolic race The pro-Western Prime Minister of the Republic of Moldova, Vasile Tofan, swam across the Bosphorus Strait in the Turkish metropolis of Istanbul on Sunday during a 6.5-kilometer race. The Prime Minister is currently on a private visit to Turkey and took part in the event alongside his 14-year-old son. “The race started on the Asian continent and ended on the European one, exactly in the direction the Republic of Moldova is heading”, Tofan wrote, quoted by media outlets in Chișinău. The travel expenses for the Prime Minister, his family members, and his team were fully covered by personal funds. The Istanbul competition reached its 38 th edition this year, organized annually by the Turkish Olympic Committee. The intercontinental Bosphorus cross-continental swim is recognized as one of the most spectacular open-water events in the world, drawing over 2,400 swimmers from numerous countries each year. Maritime traffic through the Bosphorus Strait is fully suspended for the duration of the race. https://www.dw.com/en/ethiopia-fighting-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5N83U Ethiopian government forces have come under renewed attack at regional airports across Tigray as well as positions in Afar and Amhara Image: Minasse Wondimu Hailu/Anadolu Agency/picture alliance Advertisement Rebels from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) have reportedly taken control of regional airports in Tigray, in northern Ethiopia , and further clashed with government forces in the neighboring Afar and Amhara regions. Wednesday's clashes are the latest of several in recent months and have sparked fears of renewed intense fighting in the war-ravaged region. The African Union (AU) estimates that some 600,000 people were killed in fighting between the TPLF and Ethiopian forces during a 2020-2022 civil war and that more than 1 million people remain displaced. On Wednesday, state-owned Ethiopian Airlines announced that it had canceled service at Mekelle, Tigray's capital, as well as Axum and Shire regional airports "due to the current situation." Local witnesses reported that TPLF rebels armed with light weapons had taken Mekelle Airport — which is normally controlled by government forces — without a fight. Renewed fighting comes just days after the TPLF announced that it had entered an "Alliance for Survival" with other groups aimed at removing Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and his government from power. Abiy and his Prosperity Party won reelection in June , though the vote was boycotted by Ethiopia's main opposition groups. The TPLF ruled Ethiopia from 1991 until 2018, when it was replaced by Abiy, whose election sparked the country's civil war. The Pretoria Peace Agreement brought an end to the conflict, but peace has remained elusive, with government troops resuming drone strikes in 2025 as TPLF rebels began amassing troops at regional borders. Ethiopia has accused the TPLF of allying with neighboring Eritrea and other armed groups. An advisor to Prime Minister Abiy called Wednesday's development "heartbreaking," saying rebels had launched offensives against government forces in Afar and Amhara as well as taking control of airports in Tigray. However, the Tigray army "has been instructed to counter the attack and genocidal invasion launched against us, and has entered into a defensive battle," the Tigray government said in a statement on Facebook. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/min.text: The Budapest Times Minister signals crackdown on construction firms over public procurement irregularities The government will take action against construction industry players where serious irregularities are suspected in connection with previous public procurement procedures, the Minister of Transport and Investment said on Wednesday in the Della podcast of 24.hu, confirming that emblematic figures of the NER may be involved. Dávid Vitézy stated that the state cannot declare a goal of pushing the companies of Lőrinc Mészáros and László Szíjj out of the market — at most, it can enforce the legal consequences against those who did not comply with public procurement or other regulations, which may include exclusion from future public procurements. “Among the construction industry players linked to the previous government, there are some where we already see indications of serious enough irregularities in previous public procurement procedures that we will be taking action in the coming weeks,” he said. He emphasized that the government is not acting against them because they are “unsympathetic,” but because they colluded and committed irregularities that harm the national economic interests of the country and jeopardize EU funds. At the same time, it is in Hungary’s interest that Hungarian-owned, typically medium-sized construction companies receive opportunities, and that the government structures its tenders in a way that does not favor only the largest players. This could mean breaking tenders into smaller parts or applying less stringent reference requirements, he indicated. He added that the preferences of previous years have been eliminated, meaning there will be companies in the railway, above-ground construction, or civil engineering sectors that will not be competitive without a “tailwind.” Speaking about the 2027 budget, he said the goal is for the government to fulfil as many of Tisza Party’s election promises as possible in the shortest time possible, while also keeping an eye on budgetary balance. The significant trust now gained from market players represents a considerable reduction in the burden on the budget and the Hungarian economy, but this must be carefully maintained, he warned. “The expectation towards the ministries is that (…) we look at where we can save from the waste we have inherited,” he said. Speaking about his ministry’s 2027 budget, he said it will grow by an amount in the order of 100 billion forints, primarily thanks to EU funds. He identified one of its main goals as improving the “criminally poor road conditions” in rural areas. He added that in the railway sector, 5 billion euros in EU funding provides greater room for manoeuvre, with plans to launch new vehicle tenders for the HÉV and Intercity services, and to initiate major railway development investments on main lines. The government will spend in the order of 100 billion on the development of public roads. He said the three largest items from this are the Mohács bridge, the M49 motorway, and the M1 motorway investment. The budgetary room for manoeuvre sets the limits on the plans, he noted, adding that a bridge renovation programme spanning three to four years is also being planned. In response to the question of which companies would carry out these works, he raised the possibility of developing the in-house construction capacity of Magyar Közút Zrt. and MÁV, which would allow smaller-scale renovations to be handled internally. According to him, Fidesz is falsely attempting to create the impression that only foreign companies now win infrastructure tenders, and he backed this claim with several examples. The minister also noted that on the Budapest–Belgrade railway line, domestic passenger services could begin within a few weeks, while international services could start in December.
